title: Operator capacity command removes too many storage nodes; dependent services fail on object reads/writes
source_note: Failure pattern and root-cause shape follow the AWS S3 2017-02-28 us-east-1 outage (a debugging command run with an incorrect argument removed more capacity than intended, forcing a multi-hour subsystem restart and breaking dependent services). Service names, log lines, metrics, node counts, and timestamps are fabricated for evaluation.
incident_report: Starting ~18:07 UTC, media-api is returning 500s on most requests and image uploads are failing. The web app shows broken images site-wide. Nothing was deployed to media-api or uploads-worker recently. Platform team was doing some storage maintenance earlier in the hour.

signal_lines.msg: operator session opened: planned capacity maintenance on index tier
index subsystem dropped below quorum; entering recovery mode
object-store PUT timed out after 30s; upload queue backing up (depth=8200)
index and placement subsystems require full restart; estimated recovery 3-4h
serving stale objects from CDN cache where available; write path still failing

ground_truth.root_cause: During planned index-tier capacity maintenance, an operator ran a capacity-removal command with an incorrect argument and removed 48 storage nodes instead of 4. That dropped the object-store index subsystem below quorum, forcing a multi-hour full restart of the index and placement subsystems. Every service depending on object reads and writes (media-api, uploads-worker) failed or degraded until object-store recovered.
evidence_path: object-store WARN at 18:05: capacity removal command executed with nodes_removed=48 (requested=4)
object-store index subsystem drops below quorum and enters recovery at 18:06
media-api and uploads-worker begin failing object-store GET/PUT calls at 18:07-18:08
object-store CRITICAL at 18:10: index and placement subsystems need a full multi-hour restart
ground_truth.fix: Complete the subsystem restart / restore the removed capacity. Add guardrails to the capacity tooling: cap how many nodes a single command can remove, require second-operator confirmation above a threshold, and refuse execution when the removal would take a subsystem below quorum.
